source: Not findings. Four paces at which a household can walk the same road to the same tiers, each a rule about how much of take-home is saved. The owner asked for them by name (D-235): the scenic route, the death march, and the road as it is; coasting is the Coast FIRE variant read as a route.
confidenceNote: The shares are teaching devices, not advice. Half of today's saving and spending only the floor are the two ends people actually describe; nothing here says either is right for you.
note: Read by engines/journey.js. A route is a `pace` rule: `current` saves what the household saves today (Tier0.savingsRate); `share` saves that share of today's saving; `floor` spends only the FAT floor (Schema.fatNeedsCents, D-197) and saves the rest of take-home, falling back to `floorShareFallback` of today's spending until food, a roof and getting around are typed (the same fallback Lean FIRE uses); `coast` saves at today's pace until the Coast rung and then stops, arriving at the coast target age from data/fire_variants.json. Every year figure comes from engines/projection.js yearsToTargetCents, the one loop the app has.

routes.label: The road as it is
routes.line: Save what you save now, and keep walking.

routes.label: The scenic route
routes.line: Save half of what you save now; the other half is spent on the years between.

routes.label: The death march
routes.line: Spend only the floor: food, a roof, getting around. Everything else goes in.

routes.label: Coast, then cruise
routes.line: Save at today's pace until the Coast rung, then stop adding and let it grow to the finish.
